title: Russian Pirozhki Buns with Beef and Cheddar
summary: Soft, cheese-flecked yeasted dough is wrapped around a savoury beef and cheddar filling and baked to golden, pillowy buns.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl)
2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
large egg, beaten with 1 tbsp water, for glazing

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix and knead the flour, cheddar, soured cream, butter, water, eggs, sugar, salt and yeast to a soft, smooth dough, then cover in an oiled bowl and leave to rise for about 90 minutes until puffy.

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan on medium, soften the onion, then add the garlic and beef mince and cook for 5-10 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and reaching 71°C; season, stir in the parsley, cool fully, then mix in the grated cheddar.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Divide the dough into 16 pieces of about 55 g, roll into balls on lined trays, cover and rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Flatten each ball to a 12 cm round, brush with egg wash, spoon 2 tbsp filling into the centre, draw the edges up over it and pinch firmly shut.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Place the buns seam down on the trays, cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until puffy.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C, brush the buns with the remaining egg wash and bake for 15-20 minutes until golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cool for 5-10 minutes before serving, and refrigerate any leftovers.

tips: Make sure the beef reaches 71°C and the mixture is cooled fully before mixing in the cheese, so it holds its shape in the filling.
Pinch the seams firmly shut and keep them facing down so the filling stays sealed in while proving and baking.
Let the shaped buns rise until visibly puffy before baking, for a light, soft crumb.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers and eat within a couple of days, warming gently in the oven to refresh before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
